resources.string: Reading the hour-by-hour forecast for where you are.
Check your connection and open the app again.
Allow location access so the app can read the forecast for your exact spot. Your coordinates go to the weather service and nowhere else.
The sun is gentle enough today that you can be out from dawn to dusk without reaching your limit.
The sun is strong enough that even a short spell would take you past your daily limit. If you go out, cover up.
Outside %1$s so far. About %2$s left before you reach today\'s limit.
The gentlest sun of the day is at first light, so the app will suggest dawn until you tell it otherwise.
Starting at %1$s gives you %2$s outside. From first light at %3$s it would have been %4$s.
Starting at %1$s costs you nothing today — the sun is gentle enough that you are not missing anything by waking later.
Nothing left by %1$s today. The sun is down or too strong by then.
Every figure this app uses comes from a published source. None of them were chosen by the app. Here they are, so you can check them yourself.
Tells you when your outdoor time starts.
Tells you when to head back inside so you stay under your daily limit.
The alarm that rings until you dismiss it.

No amount of sun is completely free of risk — that is measured, not a disclaimer. The risk falls as the sun weakens but never reaches zero. This app finds the gentlest daylight of your day and keeps your total under a published safety limit. It is not medical advice.

An app can add alarms to your clock app but can never change or remove them afterwards — that part is closed off by Android. So these are a snapshot of today: resend them tomorrow, and delete the old ones yourself. The Alarm option above avoids all of that.
